h1: The 7 Best Key Finders Under $100 for iPhone and Android, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Key Finder Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 key finders under $100, from Apple AirTag and Tile to Samsung SmartTag2 and Chipolo, sorted by phone fit and value.
summary: The Apple AirTag 4 Pack is the key finder to buy if you carry an iPhone, and the Life360 Tile Essentials set is the best pick when the household mixes iPhone and Android. The Samsung SmartTag2 4 Pack suits Galaxy owners who want UWB and water resistance, while the UGREEN Finder Duo Air and the Chipolo Loop are the cheaper ways to cover a few more items.
intro: The most expensive mistake with a key finder is buying the tracker before checking the phone. A tag only works well inside the network your phone belongs to: an AirTag leans on Apple devices, a Samsung SmartTag2 needs a Galaxy phone, and Tile works across both but relies on its own community. Choose by phone first and by brand second, and the rest of the decision gets easy.

We reviewed eight listings from their titles and spec details and kept the seven that fit under $100, ranking them by phone compatibility, finding range and sound, water resistance, battery approach and how many tags you get per dollar. Where a listing gives little detail, we say so rather than guess at numbers.

products.name: Apple AirTag (2nd Generation) - 4 Pack: Tracker for Keychain, Wallet, and More; Locator with Sound; Simple One-Tap Setup with iPhone or iPad
products.verdict: A four-pack of second-generation AirTags with a longer Precision Finding range and one-tap iPhone setup.
products.description:
This is the second-generation AirTag in a four-tag pack, with a built-in speaker and a Precision Finding range the listing puts at up to 1.5 times the earlier model. Setup is a single tap with an iPhone or iPad, and the tag shows up in the Find My app alongside your other Apple gear.

It ranks first because the Find My network is the largest crowd of finder devices a tracker can lean on when you are away from home, and Precision Finding turns the last few metres into an arrow on screen. Four tags is also enough to cover keys, a wallet, a bag and a jacket in one purchase. It loses points only for lock-in: the tag is useless as a locator without an Apple device, and the listing shows no built-in keyring hole, so you will need an accessory holder for keys.

Buy it if every phone in your household is an iPhone. Skip it for an Android user, since the setup and the finding features simply do not extend there.
pros: Precision Finding guides you to the tag
Four tags cover keys and bags
One-tap setup on iPhone and iPad
cons: Needs a holder to hang on keys
products.idealFor: iPhone households that want several tags at once.
products.skipIf: Anyone in your household uses Android.

products.name: Life360 Tile Essentials - Bluetooth Trackers & Item Locators for Keys, Wallets, Remotes & More
products.verdict: A multi-style Tile set for keys, wallets and remotes that works with both iOS and Android.
products.description:
The Tile Essentials set bundles trackers for keys, wallets, remotes and similar items, and the listing says it works with both iOS and Android. That makes it the only mainstream option in this ranking that does not tie you to one phone brand.

It takes second place because flexibility matters in mixed households, where one person has an iPhone and the other a Pixel or a Galaxy. Tile has also been in the tracker business longer than most rivals, so its app is mature. The tradeoff is that its finding network leans on the Tile community rather than the huge Apple or Samsung fleets, and the listing offers few specs, so range and battery details are not confirmed here.

It is the right buy if a household uses both operating systems or if you might switch phone brands. Check the current listing for the exact tag styles in the set before you order.
pros: Different styles for keys and wallets
Mature app and long track record
Easy to share across a family
cons: Smaller network than Apple or Samsung
Few specs shown on the listing
products.skipIf: Everyone owns an iPhone and wants Precision Finding.

products.name: Samsung SmartTag2 (2023) Bluetooth + UWB, IP67 Water and Dust Resistant, Findable via App, 1.5 Year Battery Life (4-Pack)
products.verdict: Four UWB tags with IP67 protection and a 1.5 year battery, with one big warranty caveat.
products.description:
The SmartTag2 four-pack pairs Bluetooth with ultra-wideband for tighter directional finding on supported Galaxy phones. It is rated IP67 against dust and water and quotes a 1.5 year battery life, which is a long time between replacements for a coin-cell tracker.

It ranks third because the spec sheet is the strongest of the Android options. The listing is a Global Edition with no US warranty, so a dead tag is your problem. That keeps it below the AirTag and Tile, which are easier to support. UWB also needs a compatible Galaxy phone, so the best features are lost on a Pixel or a Motorola.

Buy it if you already own a recent Galaxy phone and want four tags with a real water rating. Skip it if you want a manufacturer warranty in the United States.
pros: IP67 rating handles rain and dust
cons: No US warranty on this edition
Best features need a Galaxy phone
products.idealFor: Galaxy owners who want sturdy, water-resistant tags.
products.skipIf: You want a US warranty or use a non-Samsung phone.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy SmartTag2, Bluetooth Tracker, Smart Tag GPS Locator Tracking Device, Item Finder for Keys, Wallet, Luggage, Pets
products.verdict: A single SmartTag2 for Android 11 or later, priced in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
This is the single-tag version of the SmartTag2, built for phones and tablets running Android 11 or later. The listing frames it as an item finder for keys, wallets, luggage and pets, and costs less than the multi-packs.

It ranks fourth because a single tag is a smaller commitment than a pack and the SmartTag2 hardware is a solid piece of kit. The listing text calls it a GPS locator, and that wording is misleading: it is a Bluetooth tag that depends on nearby phones for location, not a standalone GPS tracker with a cellular link. Keep that in mind for pets and luggage. It sits below the four-pack because buying tags one at a time costs more per tag.

Buy it if you want to add one tag to a Galaxy setup, or test the SmartTag2 before committing to a pack. Skip it if you need real-time GPS tracking for a pet.
cons: Not a true standalone GPS tracker
Costs more per tag than the pack
products.idealFor: Android users who want one tag for keys.
products.skipIf: You need live GPS for a pet or a vehicle.

products.name: UGREEN Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack (iOS and Android)
products.verdict: Four compact tags that the listing says cover both iOS and Android, for $25 to $50.
products.description:
The Finder Duo Air is a four-pack of compact tags, and the listing says it supports iOS and Android. At $25 to $50 for the whole set, it is the cheapest way here to tag several items.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives little in the way of range, battery or water details, and a lesser-known brand has a smaller finding crowd than Apple or Samsung. Cross-platform support is the draw, but it is worth confirming how each phone type connects, since platform support in trackers often means different features on each side.

It is the right buy for tagging low-stakes items such as a gym bag, a remote or a spare key. Do not rely on it for something expensive or irreplaceable.
pros: Four tags at a low price
Compact tags fit on a keyring
cons: Specs are thin on the listing
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want several cheap tags.
products.skipIf: You want to track something valuable.

products.name: Chipolo POP Tracking Tag - Colorful, Compatible, Loud Bluetooth Tracker
products.verdict: A colorful Chipolo tag with a loud speaker, sold in the $50 to $100 bracket.
products.description:
The Chipolo POP is a colorful Bluetooth tag that the listing describes as loud and compatible. The color range is a genuine usability point, since a bright tag is easier to spot on a hook or in a bag than a plain white one.

It ranks sixth because the listing shows no specs beyond the loud speaker, and the title leaves the compatibility vague. Chipolo is a respected maker, but you should confirm on the listing which network and which phones it works with before ordering, since a mismatch is the classic tracker mistake. It scores above the Chipolo Loop because the sound makes it easier to find in a messy room.

Buy it if you want a bright, noisy tag to attach to a bag or a pet carrier. Skip it if you want a documented range or battery life figure.
pros: Bright colors are easy to spot
products.idealFor: Buyers who lose items in cluttered rooms.
products.skipIf: You need confirmed range and battery numbers.

products.name: Chipolo Loop, Rechargeable Bluetooth Tracker for Key and Pocket Location
products.verdict: A rechargeable Chipolo tag for keys and pockets, in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
The Chipolo Loop is a rechargeable Bluetooth tracker designed for keys and pockets, and costs less than the multi-packs. Rechargeable is the unusual part: most rivals use a coin cell, so there is no battery to swap and no cell to buy.

It ranks last because the listing gives few details on range, sound or network, and a rechargeable tag only helps if you remember to charge it. Forgetting is easy, because a tracker that sits unused in a coat pocket for months is exactly the one that is dead when you need it. It scores a little below the POP since it is a single tag with less loudness information.

Buy it if you hate swapping coin cells and you charge your devices on a routine. Skip it if you want a set-and-forget tag that runs for a year or more.
pros: Rechargeable, no coin cell to buy
cons: Range and sound details are missing
products.idealFor: People who dislike swapping coin cells.
products.skipIf: You want a tag you never have to think about.

whatMatters.detail: A tracker does its best work inside one ecosystem. AirTag depends on Apple devices, SmartTag2 depends on Galaxy phones, and Tile and UGREEN claim both. Check the phone compatibility line near the top of the listing before looking at anything else.

When you are away from home, your tag relies on strangers' phones to report its location. Bigger networks, such as Apple's or Samsung's, find more items. Smaller brands can still help at home, but they are weaker on a train or in a parking lot.

A speaker helps you find a tag in the next room, while UWB or Precision Finding points you to it. Look for the words sound, UWB or Precision Finding on the listing. A tag with no speaker is a poor key finder.

Coin-cell tags can run a year or more, while rechargeable ones need a routine. An IP67 rating, as on the SmartTag2 pack, means the tag survives rain and brief dunking. If your keys live in a bag or a rainy coat pocket, that rating is worth paying for.

Some listings are imported versions with no US warranty, as on the SmartTag2 Global Edition. A cheap price can hide that gap. Read the product details for the word warranty before you add a pack to your cart.

faq.q: Can I use an AirTag with an Android phone?
faq.a: Not for setup or finding. The AirTag needs an iPhone or iPad to register and to use Precision Finding. If your household has Android phones, choose Tile Essentials or a Samsung tag instead.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a key finder?
faq.a: Choosing a brand before checking the phone. A tag that is not built for your phone's ecosystem will still ring, but it cannot report its location through strangers' devices, which is the feature you pay for.

faq.q: Is a four-pack worth it over a single tag?
faq.a: Usually, yes. The Apple AirTag 4 Pack and the Samsung SmartTag2 4-Pack cover keys, a wallet, a bag and a jacket for less per tag. A single tag only makes sense if you are testing a brand first.

The AirTag takes a single tap with an iPhone or iPad. Samsung and Tile tags pair through their own apps in a few minutes. Keep the phone's Bluetooth switched on during setup and register each tag with a name you will remember.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: The SmartTag2 pack quotes 1.5 years on its listing. Other tags here do not state a figure, so assume about a year for coin-cell models and plan for regular recharging on the Chipolo Loop.

faq.q: Do these work as a real GPS tracker for pets?
faq.a: No. Despite the wording on some listings, these are Bluetooth tags that depend on nearby phones. For a pet that roams, a dedicated GPS collar with a cellular plan is the better tool.

finalTake: For iPhone owners, the Apple AirTag 4 Pack is the best key finder under $100. Households that mix iPhone and Android should buy the Life360 Tile Essentials set, and Galaxy owners get the most from the Samsung SmartTag2 4-Pack, warranty gap included. The UGREEN Finder Duo Air and the Chipolo Loop are the cheaper ways to cover low-stakes items. Check your phone before you check the price.
